helpful: The provisioned BIO and petition in full text: the BIO's account of Slaughter and the Harris denial, with pin cites, did most of the work before any retrieval.
The sal-v4 band table with per-Term bracketed reached rates, which made the pooled elevated anchor a one-line computation.
The opinions endpoint's plain_text field, which served the Slaughter slip opinion when read_document and search_document reported no text for the same opinion id.
gaps: read_document / search_document returned 'No text is available' for a same-day SCOTUS slip opinion whose plain_text was populated; a fallback to plain_text inside those tools would save a 227k-character raw fetch.

CourtListener's docket search found nothing for SCOTUS docket 25-1110, so I could not check whether the Harris v. Bessent denial carried a dissent or statement, which is the single input that would most sharpen the dissent-from-denial number. A way to read supremecourt.gov order lists or SCOTUS dockets by number would fill this.

fedcourts query has no subject or keyword filter on SCOTUS rows and its --citation column is sparse (about 200 rows), so it cannot surface substantively similar cert petitions such as prior removal-power petitions and their fates.

context.distribution_count does not distinguish a redistribution after a requested response from a relist out of conference; a response_requested date on cert-stage context would let a cell read the CFR signal directly rather than from docket text.
notes: Total retrieval: 2 corpus queries, 7 MCP calls, no web search. The case's disposition does not yet exist (conference 2026-10-16), so forward mode carried no leakage risk.
